implementation_notes: Rails' ActiveRecord makes the parent the unit that is saved: accepts_nested_attributes_for on has_one/has_many turns autosave on automatically, and all changes - including the destruction of dependents marked with allow_destroy - are saved and destroyed atomically inside the parent's save transaction. composed_of covers the other half of the pattern, dependents with no table of their own that are mapped onto columns of the root, with the value object frozen so it cannot be mutated behind the mapping's back. Keep the nested models thin: they travel as one params hash and are validated together with the parent.
code_sketch:
class Order < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :lines, dependent: :destroy
  accepts_nested_attributes_for :lines, allow_destroy: true
  composed_of :total, class_name: "Money", mapping: { total_cents: :amount }
end

order.update(lines_attributes: [{ id: 1, qty: 2 }, { id: 2, _destroy: "1" }])
# parent, children and destruction commit atomically
pitfalls: allow_destroy is off by default, so nested updates look like deletions while the row survives; the _destroy key is silently ignored.
Destroying a child requires its id in the hash, otherwise Rails raises RecordNotFound instead of treating the entry as a new record.
A composed_of value object is frozen: mutating it in place raises RuntimeError and nothing is persisted.
